title: Does the knowledge reward matter? Step by step, with and without

design.question: Does paying a knowledge reward (1 per new bit, flowing back with α) change how far a society gets, and when?
design.compare: the knowledge reward on (1 per new bit) and off (0), at each step of the model and each α
design.fixed: everything else in each step experiment (6 × 8 generated graphs, 12 agents, budget 1,200); the same graphs and luck with and without

answer: With sharing set by the rules and equal money (step 1), the knowledge reward changes nothing. Once agents choose what to share and money follows earnings (steps 3-5), it matters at high α: at α = 0.8 a society solves 1.8 of 2 targets with it and 0.4 without (step 3). At α = 0.2 or 0 it barely matters: flowing value back already pays for intermediate work.
caveats: Exploratory, not fixed in advance: a first look with 40 runs per point came first (2026-11-06); this is the same comparison with more runs.
"Clear" means the paired difference is more than two standard errors from zero.
Step 1 has no α = 0 row; its open societies set β = 1, so sharing is fixed at 100%.

Why it matters for the Lean runs: there, money does not follow earnings and labs do not choose what to publish (like step 1), so on these results a knowledge reward would change little until money follows earnings.
